_meta.title: Item Flavor — Realm of Eldoria
_meta.voice: THEME §7 — warm gravitas, child-safe; Studio-Ghibli mentor cadence
_meta.convention: Each entry mirrors an Items.gd id. 'flavor' is the canonical hand-painted tooltip body — a single short paragraph, never more than three sentences. 'whisper' is an optional rarer second line a UI may surface on long-hover (max one short sentence). 'attribution' names the in-world voice the line belongs to (a Briarwood NPC, a scribe's hand, or 'narrator' for the village-eye). 'origin' anchors the item to canon (faction, place, or NPC). 'glossary' lists any Old Faerie / Stone-Tongue words used, with their canonical sense. Add only when the item is touched by canon — not every weapon needs a glossary entry.

old_faerie_introduced_this_artifact.sense: the holding-warm — a thing that has held warmth long enough to remember it: a banked fire at first light, a hand-me-down cloak, a tea cup at the third sip
twice-given — an object that was a gift before it was a hand-me-down; the gentlest word for a thing worn first by someone who loved you
the keeping-edge — the patience of a blade whose edge does not blunt, because someone hones it every Foxthaw without fail; said also of the keeping of small promises

withholding_ledger: No item names the Steppe-rider of the Crystal-Caves fragment, nor the kin he came south to find.
Cailen's Horseshoe (Maeve's hearth piece) is referenced obliquely as a hook only; it is not made an in-bag item this run.
No item references what lies past the Whisperwood forest-line.
No item invents a fourth Stone-Tongue word; the cap holds at three.
canon_anchors_used: lore/world.md (Sundering, Three Crowns, Wild Pantheon, Calendar, Tongues)
lore/npcs/smith_edda.md (Brigid's mark, the haethe, Halsa's anvil, the unnamed dream-blood)
lore/npcs/stablemaster_roan.md (Briar's Run, the courier-string, kerrithen as practice)
lore/npcs/elder_maeve.md (Vigil candles, the eighty-ninth knot, the Stag-Court's offer declined)

rusty_sword.name: Rusty Sword
rusty_sword.flavor: Found half-buried at the edge of a barley field, hilt-leather long since taken by the rain. Edda will say only that it was forged before her time and that the smith who made it meant well. It still cuts. Most things mean well, in their first work.
rusty_sword.whisper: A first blade is not for the wielder. It is the village remembering how to send someone out.

iron_sword.name: Iron Sword
iron_sword.flavor: Edda's standard work — straight, honest, weighted to the elbow rather than the wrist. She quenches it in pond-water on the morning after a Foxthaw, and the pond-water remembers. Hone it once a season and it will keep its thrennen for as long as you do.
iron_sword.whisper: *Edda, without looking up:* "Bring it back when the song goes flat. I can hear it from the doorway."

glossary.sense: the keeping-edge — said of a blade honed every Foxthaw without fail

steel_blade.name: Steel Blade
steel_blade.flavor: A haethe-blade — quenched on a midsummer night by a smith who had finally let herself weep at the anvil. It rings true if you set the flat against your knuckle and listen. Edda will not name the price she paid to forge it; if you ask, she will hand you stew instead.
steel_blade.whisper: Brigid the Forge-Mother kept this promise.
steel_blade.origin: Briarwood forge, Edda-made; the first blade that rang true after Halsa

glossary.sense: the song iron remembers — the faint hum a properly-tempered blade gives off when struck

frost_saber.name: Frost Saber
frost_saber.flavor: Smiths who name a saber Frost know what they are naming. The Pale Wyrm sleeps somewhere deep beneath the world, and its dreaming pushes cold up through certain blades. Edda has only forged two of these in her life, and laid the second one down at a cairn before it could be named.
frost_saber.whisper: Vellum the Patient Stone holds the breath this blade was cooled in.

glossary.sense: memory of stone — a place where time pools

ember_axe.name: Ember Axe
ember_axe.flavor: Forged hot-side, the way Brigid likes it — bellows working, sparks high enough to read by, the smith laughing for the first time that season. Edda made this one for a Stag-night offering and a courier's brother bought it before the candle had cooled.
ember_axe.whisper: Brigid the Forge-Mother keeps her promises in fire that has not yet been banked.

shadow_dagger.name: Shadow Dagger
shadow_dagger.flavor: A crossroads blade, of the kind Erris of the Two Roads is said to bless if you leave a coin in the road-dust the night you carry it. Single-edged, dark-quenched, balanced for the hand that does not need to swing twice. Honest enough work; honest enough use, depending.
shadow_dagger.whisper: Erris keeps no books. The coin in the dust is the whole receipt.

dragonfang.name: Dragonfang
dragonfang.flavor: Older than oath. The Wild Pantheon names it the Wyrm's parting gift; the Stone Crown's riders, more practically, call it the long tooth. It hums lower than any haethe Edda has known, and on cold mornings it sings to the mountains in a voice the mountains seem to answer.
dragonfang.whisper: Vellum's spine remembers what bit it.

cloth.name: Cloth Tunic
cloth.flavor: Hemmed twice — once by a mother for a child, once by the child for a smaller cousin. Linen this soft is haelen: it has held warmth for someone before you, and it remembers. Lyra leaves a sprig of marshmint in the folds without thinking.
cloth.whisper: What is haelen does not need to be told it is loved.

glossary.sense: the holding-warm — a thing that has held warmth long enough to remember it

leather.name: Leather Vest
leather.flavor: Cut from saddler-stock — tooled small along the inside seam in the way Roan's father Tael used to. Mor-vaere, in the older speech: it was a gift before it was a hand-me-down. Roan does not say so when he sells one. He tips his head and finishes the strap he is drawing through a buckle.
leather.whisper: *Roan, adjusting a strap:* "Aye. It'll wear. Bring it back when the buckle goes."

glossary.sense: twice-given — an object that was a gift before it was a hand-me-down

chainmail.name: Chainmail
chainmail.flavor: Ring-shirt of southern make — Iron Crown work, three years on the road before it ever reached this valley. The little kink at the left shoulder is where a courier was unhorsed and lived to tell. Edda has retempered the rivets; Roan has restitched the under-tunic; it is, by careful arithmetic, more Briarwood than Iron Crown now.
chainmail.whisper: Three hands have kept this ring-shirt. The fourth is yours.

steel_plate.name: Steel Plate
steel_plate.flavor: Smoke-city work — the spaulders bear an Iron Crown stamp the polish has nearly forgiven. Heavy in the way honest plate is heavy: it asks you to carry it on the long walk, not the short sprint. Edda has rivetted a small Brigid-mark inside the breast where no one but the wearer will ever see.
steel_plate.whisper: Brigid keeps the small marks no one else looks for.
steel_plate.origin: Iron Crown make; Edda-marked at the seam

emberforge.name: Emberforge Plate
emberforge.flavor: Quenched in a coal-bed Edda banked seven days before striking — the longest-banked fire of her working life. There is a single drop of the smith's own blood hammered into the breastplate, where her thumb-scar tells. She has never said so. She will never say so. The plate carries it anyway.
emberforge.whisper: Brigid the Forge-Mother's promise, this one, is kept twice.

dragonscale.name: Dragonscale
dragonscale.flavor: A scale shed in the Pale Wyrm's deep sleep — found on the lip of a thirre where the cave-air smells of cold iron, and not where any honest courier ever rode. Heavier than it looks. Older than the village. The green of moss that has never been walked on.
dragonscale.whisper: The Sundering is still happening, slowly, where this came from.
dragonscale.origin: Pre-Sundering; Pale Wyrm-shed; Crystal Caves verge

glossary.sense: memory of stone — a place where time pools

ring_focus.name: Ring of Focus
ring_focus.flavor: A scribe's ring — copper, hammered thin, a sliver of crystal-shard set into the bezel where most rings would carry a stone. The shard is from the Caves. The hammering is Edda's. The setting is Mara's southern jeweler. Three hands, one ring; the village calls that lucky.
ring_focus.whisper: Erris of the Two Roads passes a coin between three hands and counts it once.

talisman_oak.name: Oak Talisman
talisman_oak.flavor: A disc cut from an oak that fell of its own weight in the deep Whisperwood — Lyra harvested the wood with her hands in the leaf-mould and apologized aloud to Thiar the Stag before she touched it. Strung on a cord she dyed in marshmint water. Worn next to the skin, it warms quickly. That is haelen, she will say, and not magic.
talisman_oak.whisper: *Lyra, both hands on the cord:* "Thiar lent the wood. We hold it for him."

crit_amulet.name: Hawk's Amulet
crit_amulet.flavor: Steppe work — a single hawk-bone bead between two rings of braided horsehair. The Stone Crown's riders carry these on the Foxthaw passes, where the wind takes a careless rider and the hawk does not. Roan has one of his own that he never wears. He will sell you this one fairly. He will not look at it as you put it on.
crit_amulet.whisper: *Roan, tipping his head:* "Wear it on the road. Take it off at table."

guardian_core.name: Guardian's Core
guardian_core.flavor: A Crystal-Cave heart-stone, taken only from a guardian whose vigil had ended. It hums at the same low pitch as Vellum the Patient Stone is said to hum on the deepest Longnight nights. Edda will not work it. Lyra will not crush it. Maeve would set it at the back of the Vigil shelf and let it hum quietly through any winter that needed it.
guardian_core.whisper: Vellum has not gone anywhere. Vellum is listening.

glossary.sense: memory of stone — a place where time pools

hp_potion_s.name: Lesser Health Potion
hp_potion_s.flavor: Heart's-ease for what aches inside; dogwort for what aches outside; marshmint for both — pressed warm in a small clay flask sealed with beeswax and a thumbprint. Lyra's basic, sold at honest cost. The thumbprint is hers. She presses it last so the wax remembers.
hp_potion_s.whisper: *Lyra, both hands on yours:* "You don't have to tell me which yet. I can read you."

hp_potion_l.name: Greater Health Potion
hp_potion_l.flavor: Lyra's thalen-ai salve — heart's-ease, dogwort, marshmint, and the seventh herb she will not name except in the older constructions. Reserved for the long road and the bad night. She does not sell this one to strangers; if it is in your hand, the village has decided about you.
hp_potion_l.whisper: *Lyra, very softly:* "Thalen-ai. The land trusted us this season. Bring back the jar."
hp_potion_l.origin: Briarwood herb-shed; Lyra-pressed; Wennet's coat-pocket recipe

glossary.sense: the herb that grows where it is needed — both plant and grace

mp_potion.name: Mana Draught
mp_potion.flavor: A stargaze brew — distilled on a clear Honeysong night with the still set under the open sky, so the steam and the starlight could meet at the lid. Bards leave a coin for Erris of the Two Roads at every crossroads; Lyra leaves the first sip of every batch at the well.
mp_potion.whisper: Erris keeps the songs that do not yet have endings.

glossary.sense: the long path — both the river of stars across the night sky and a mortal's life from cradle to cairn

wolf_pelt.name: Wolf Pelt
wolf_pelt.flavor: A dire-wolf's winter coat, harvested with the hunter's apology made aloud — the mercy owed to prey, in Thiar the Stag's older speech. Lyra cures these with bark-tannin and lays them flat under a board for a fortnight. They keep haelen the way good linen does.
wolf_pelt.whisper: *Lyra, kneeling:* "The land trusted us. Say so."

wolf_fang.name: Wolf Fang
wolf_fang.flavor: A small ivory tooth, shed-edge polished by use rather than by smith. Roan keeps a clean one in the corner of his strap-tin and will not say why; pressed for a price, he will tip his head and finish the buckle he is drawing through. Take it as bounty if you must. He would rather you took it as a question.
wolf_fang.whisper: *Roan, not looking up:* "Aye. The forest-line tonight. Mind it."

goblin_ear.name: Goblin Ear
goblin_ear.flavor: Bounty token, payable to Mara the Merchant in honest coin and at posted rate. The Whisperwood goblins were once something else, before the Sundering — a scholar might tell you so, and Lyra might agree by a small silence. Mara takes the ear and the silence both, and writes the count down without comment.
goblin_ear.whisper: *Mara, weighing coin:* "Six. Honest count, honest pay. Mind the road."

crystal_shard.name: Crystal Shard
crystal_shard.flavor: A shard of the Caves — cool to the skin, faintly humming on cold mornings the way Vellum the Patient Stone is said to hum on the deepest Longnight. Edda will reforge a blade for a fistful of these. She will not say where she lays the dust the grindstone makes; only that the dust is not hers to throw away.
crystal_shard.whisper: *Edda, hammer-clang:* "Bring me five and the kettle's already on."

glossary.sense: memory of stone — a place where time pools
to lay something down so the land may hold it

warlord_horn.name: Warlord's Horn
warlord_horn.flavor: The Goblin Warlord's signal-horn — bull's horn rimmed in beaten iron, banner-cord still knotted where the standard was torn away. Mara will buy it at full price and never ask where it came from. Maeve, who has a longer memory, will look at it once and not again.
warlord_horn.whisper: Trouble brews in the Whisperwood. The horn will not call again.
